intro: がてら and かたわら both put two activities together, at very different scales. がてら is one outing serving two purposes: you go out to do A and, since you are out anyway, you do B too. かたわら is a double life: alongside a main job or role, someone keeps up another activity over months or years.

skills.rule: Action noun or verb stem + がてら + verb of going: doing A, and using the same outing to do B.
skills.explain:
AがてらB: you set out to do A and use that same trip to do B as well. A is a noun of action attached directly (散歩, 買い物, 見物, 運動, 出張) or a verb stem (送り, 行き). B is usually a verb of movement or a visit: 行く, 寄る, 出かける, 見てくる. 散歩がてらパンを買ってきた: I went for a walk and picked up bread while I was at it. A is the occasion; B is what you fold into it.

Both parts belong to one occasion, done by the same person, and usually by choice. がてら takes no の after a noun.

Edges: かたわら is a long-running second activity, not a trip (会社に勤めるかたわら小説を書く). ながら is two actions at the same moment (歩きながら話す); がてら needs only the same outing, not the same moment. かたがた is a formal relative for courtesy visits and letters: お礼かたがたご挨拶に伺います.
patterns: [散歩 / 買い物 / 見物 / 出張] がてら [行く / 寄る / 見てくる]

examples.jp: 散歩[さんぽ]{がてら}、コンビニに行[い]ってきます。
examples.en: I'm going for a walk, and I'll drop by the convenience store.

examples.jp: 買[か]い物[もの]{がてら}、駅前[えきまえ]の新[あたら]しい店[みせ]を見[み]てきた。
examples.en: While I was out shopping, I checked out the new shop by the station.

examples.jp: 運動[うんどう]{がてら}、毎朝[まいあさ]歩[ある]いて会社[かいしゃ]に行[い]っています。
examples.en: I walk to work every morning, partly for the exercise.

examples.jp: 友達[ともだち]を駅[えき]まで送[おく]り{がてら}、本屋[ほんや]に寄[よ]った。
examples.en: I walked my friend to the station and stopped at a bookshop on the way.

examples.jp: 出張[しゅっちょう]{がてら}、京都[きょうと]の紅葉[こうよう]を見[み]てきました。
examples.en: On a business trip, I took the chance to see the autumn leaves in Kyoto.

contrast.note: 仕事のかたわら絵を描く is an ongoing parallel activity. 散歩がてら is one outing. If it covers months or years, it is かたわら.
歩きながら電話する: the same moment. 散歩がてら本屋に寄る: the same outing, not necessarily the same moment. がてら almost always comes with a verb of going.
お礼かたがた伺う is formal and limited to polite purposes (お礼, ご挨拶, お見舞い). In everyday sentences use がてら.

mistakes.bad: テレビを見[み]{がてら}ご飯[はん]を食[た]べた。
mistakes.good: テレビを見[み]{ながら}ご飯[はん]を食[た]べた。
mistakes.note: Two actions at the same moment take ながら. がてら needs an outing that serves a second purpose.

mistakes.bad: 会社員[かいしゃいん]{がてら}小説[しょうせつ]を書[か]いている。
mistakes.good: 会社[かいしゃ]に勤[つと]める{かたわら}、小説[しょうせつ]を書[か]いている。
mistakes.note: A long-term side activity alongside a job is かたわら.

mistakes.bad: 散歩[さんぽ]の{がてら}、パンを買[か]ってきた。
mistakes.good: 散歩[さんぽ]{がてら}、パンを買[か]ってきた。
mistakes.note: がてら attaches directly to the noun, with no の.

skills.tip: Can you say since I'm out anyway, I'll also...? がてら. Doing both at this very moment is ながら.

skills.rule: N の / V-dictionary + かたわら: alongside a main occupation, the same person keeps up another activity over time.
skills.explain:
AかたわらB: A is someone's main work or role, and B is something they also do on the side, regularly and over a long period. A is a noun + の (仕事のかたわら, 学業のかたわら) or a verb in the dictionary form (会社に勤めるかたわら). B is a sustained activity: 小説を書く, ボランティアを続ける, 子供にサッカーを教える.

It describes how someone lives, so it suits profiles, biographies and news. A and B have the same subject. It is not used for a single occasion, and not for two things done at the same moment.

The noun 傍ら also means beside, as in 道の傍らに (by the side of the road); that is a place noun, not this pattern.

Edges: がてら joins two purposes in one outing (散歩がてら). ながら is simultaneous (歩きながら). 一方で contrasts two sides of anything; かたわら specifically adds a side activity to a main one.
patterns: [job / studies] の かたわら [ongoing activity]

examples.jp: 父[ちち]は仕事[しごと]の{かたわら}、ボランティアを続[つづ]けている。
examples.en: My father keeps up his volunteering alongside his job.

examples.jp: 姉[あね]は大学[だいがく]に通[かよ]う{かたわら}、カフェでアルバイトをしている。
examples.en: My sister works part-time at a café while attending university.

examples.jp: 山田[やまだ]さんは会社[かいしゃ]に勤[つと]める{かたわら}、小説[しょうせつ]を書[か]いている。
examples.en: Yamada writes novels while holding down a company job.

examples.jp: 佐藤[さとう]さんは医師[いし]として働[はたら]く{かたわら}、地域[ちいき]の子供[こども]たちにサッカーを教[おし]えている。
examples.en: Besides working as a doctor, Sato teaches football to local children.

examples.jp: その作家[さっか]は教職[きょうしょく]の{かたわら}、三十年[さんじゅうねん]で百冊[ひゃくさつ]以上[いじょう]の本[ほん]を書[か]いた。
examples.en: Alongside teaching, the writer produced over a hundred books in thirty years.

contrast.note: がてら: one trip, two purposes (買い物がてら). かたわら: two activities kept up side by side over time.
ながら is the same moment, with any action. かたわら is never about the same moment; nobody writes a novel at the instant they are at the office.
つつ is literary ながら (while, or although). It does not mean as a side activity.

mistakes.bad: 散歩[さんぽ]の{かたわら}、パンを買[か]った。
mistakes.good: 散歩[さんぽ]{がてら}、パンを買[か]った。
mistakes.note: One outing used for a second purpose is がてら. かたわら needs an ongoing main activity.

mistakes.bad: 音楽[おんがく]を聞[き]く{かたわら}宿題[しゅくだい]をした。
mistakes.good: 音楽[おんがく]を聞[き]き{ながら}宿題[しゅくだい]をした。
mistakes.note: Doing two things at the same moment is ながら.

mistakes.bad: 仕事[しごと]{かたわら}、絵[え]を描[か]いている。
mistakes.good: 仕事[しごと]の{かたわら}、絵[え]を描[か]いている。
mistakes.note: After a noun, かたわら needs の.

skills.tip: Is it a profile sentence: besides being X, they have also done Y for years? かたわら. One trip is がてら.
